scholarships.description: Awards selected Latino college students $5,000 toward their education plus a weekend Leadership Development Seminar and recognition at the annual gala. Open to Illinois residents including those without immigration status and DACA recipients who have not previously received the award.

scholarships.name: ILACHE Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Illinois Latino Council on Higher Education (ILACHE)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Latino graduating high school seniors and undergraduates who will enroll full time at an Illinois college or university. Recognizes academic achievement and community involvement.

scholarships.name: Hispanic Lawyers Scholarship Fund of Illinois
scholarships.organization: Hispanic Lawyers Scholarship Fund of Illinois (HLSF)
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Latino law students and pre law students with ties to Illinois who are pursuing legal education. Supports tuition and related expenses for those committed to serving the community.

scholarships.name: Chicago Urban League Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarships for recent high school seniors and returning students up to age 21 continuing their postsecondary education, with a focus on opening opportunity for African American students. Awards range from $1,000 to $10,000.

scholarships.name: Chicago Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship established to help graduating Chicago high school students who show desire to succeed but may not meet merit based academic thresholds. Covers tuition, fees and books not covered by other aid plus a stipend totaling $4,000 per academic year.

scholarships.name: JACL Chicago Scholarship Program
scholarships.organization: Japanese American Citizens League, Chicago Chapter
scholarships.description: Scholarships for students entering or attending accredited colleges and universities full time in the United States. Applicants do not need to be JACL members and awards support students connected to the Chicago area.

scholarships.name: AABA of Greater Chicago Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Asian American Bar Association of Greater Chicago Foundation
scholarships.description: Awards at least one scholarship to a law student who has demonstrated commitment to serving the Asian Pacific American community through public interest or public service legal work. A connection to the Chicago area is preferred.

scholarships.name: Diversity Scholarship Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Chicago area law students from diverse and historically underrepresented backgrounds. Recipients are recognized at the annual Unity Award Gala.

scholarships.name: Luminarts Cultural Foundation Fellowship
scholarships.organization: Luminarts Cultural Foundation (Union League Club of Chicago)
scholarships.description: Competitive fellowships supporting young Chicago area artists, writers and musicians in visual arts, creative writing, classical music and jazz improvisation. Fellows receive financial support and ongoing cultivation by the foundation.

scholarships.name: Evans Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Western Golf Association / Evans Scholars Foundation
scholarships.description: Full tuition and housing college scholarship for high achieving caddies with a strong two year caddie record and limited financial means. Illinois caddies are geographically eligible and awards are renewable across four years.

scholarships.name: Illinois AMVETS Scholarship
scholarships.description: Financial assistance for Illinois veterans, active duty service members and their dependents pursuing higher education. Awards up to $2,000 can be used for tuition, fees, books and housing. Application window runs November 1 to March 1.

scholarships.name: American Legion Department of Illinois Scholarships
scholarships.description: Several scholarships offered by the American Legion Department of Illinois for Illinois students, including awards tied to veteran family connections. Supports tuition and educational costs for graduating seniors and current students.

scholarships.name: IAA Foundation College Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships from the charitable arm of the Illinois Farm Bureau for Illinois farm families and Farm Bureau members, spouses or children majoring in agriculture or ag related fields. Selection weighs activities, community involvement, career goals and financial plan. Application window runs January 1 to February 15.

scholarships.name: Cook County Farm Bureau Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Cook County Farm Bureau member families pursuing college study. Supports graduating high school seniors and current college students from the Cook County area.

scholarships.name: DuPage County Farm Bureau Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for DuPage County students connected to Farm Bureau member families pursuing higher education. Supports graduating seniors and current college students in the DuPage County area.

scholarships.name: Farm Credit Illinois Agriculture Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Illinois students pursuing agriculture related degrees, awarded across the Farm Credit Illinois territory. In a recent cycle the program awarded $75,000 among selected Illinois students.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation of Central Illinois Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarship program serving Central Illinois students through a Universal Application requiring a transcript, financial information and essay questions. Most scholarships open the first week of January and are due the first Wednesday of March.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for the Land of Lincoln Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Community Foundation for the Land of Lincoln
scholarships.description: Administers roughly 50 scholarship funds for students across Cass, Christian, Logan, Macoupin, Menard, Montgomery, Morgan and Sangamon counties in central Illinois. A recent cycle awarded about $230,000 across 102 scholarships and renewals.

scholarships.name: Rockford Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Awards scholarships to students who live in the greater Rockford area and have been accepted to a college, university or program of higher education. Applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.

scholarships.name: DuPage Foundation Scholarship Funds
scholarships.description: The DuPage Foundation maintains multiple named scholarship funds for students in the DuPage County area. Students are advised to check with their high school or college guidance office for available Foundation scholarships.

scholarships.name: CHA Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Scholarship for current Chicago Housing Authority residents listed on a lease who are pursuing postsecondary education. The application for the school year opens in late January.

scholarships.name: CSBG Scholarship Program
scholarships.organization: City of Chicago Department of Family and Support Services
scholarships.description: Helps low income Chicago residents who meet CSBG income eligibility finance higher education at an Illinois college, university or vocational training program. Awards support tuition and related educational costs.

scholarships.name: Illinois Restaurant Association Educational Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school and college students pursuing culinary and hospitality degrees at colleges and universities. Awards support tuition and program costs for students entering the food service industry.

scholarships.name: Illinois CPA Society Accounting Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: Academic scholarships for accounting students who plan to sit for the CPA exam in Illinois within three years. Applicants must attend an Illinois college or university, hold at least a 3.0 GPA and be a US citizen or permanent resident. Includes general awards plus named awards for Black, women and other students.

scholarships.name: City Colleges of Chicago Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for City Colleges of Chicago students, the majority of which require living in the city of Chicago. Fall applications for the academic year are due in late September with a spring deadline in March.

scholarships.name: IHSA Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships from the charitable foundation of the Illinois High School Association recognizing Illinois high school students for achievement and participation. Supports graduating seniors continuing to college.

scholarships.name: Michigan Achievement Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Michigan Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential (MiLEAP) / MI Student Aid
scholarships.description: State scholarship for recent Michigan high school graduates who enroll at a Michigan college within 15 months of graduation and show financial need with a Student Aid Index of $30,000 or less. Amounts vary by institution type, up to $5,500 per year at public universities.

scholarships.name: Michigan Competitive Scholarship
scholarships.organization: MI Student Aid (Michigan Department of Treasury)
scholarships.description: Need- and merit-based award for Michigan residents attending eligible Michigan colleges who meet a qualifying SAT score and file the FAFSA. Renewable if the student maintains satisfactory academic progress.

scholarships.name: Michigan Tuition Grant
scholarships.organization: MI Student Aid (Michigan Department of Treasury)
scholarships.description: Need-based grant for Michigan residents attending eligible private, nonprofit Michigan colleges and universities who demonstrate financial need through the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: Michigan Fostering Futures Scholarship
scholarships.organization: MI Student Aid (Michigan Department of Treasury)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for students who were in Michigan foster care after their 13th birthday and are attending an eligible Michigan public or private college. Funds are paid toward on-campus housing, tuition, fees, books, and other costs.

scholarships.name: Children of Veterans Tuition Grant
scholarships.organization: State of Michigan / MI Student Aid
scholarships.description: Undergraduate tuition assistance for Michigan residents who are children of a Michigan veteran who is totally and permanently disabled, deceased, or missing in action as a result of military service. Renewable for up to four years.

scholarships.name: Grand Rapids Community Foundation General Scholarship
scholarships.description: One general online application matches West Michigan students to more than 100 scholarships totaling over $300,000 each year. Open to high school seniors, current college students, and nontraditional and vocational learners with a connection to West Michigan.

scholarships.name: Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan Scholarships
scholarships.description: A single application at the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan is considered for dozens of scholarships for students across Detroit and the surrounding southeast Michigan counties. Account registration is required before the mid-February registration deadline.

scholarships.name: Kalamazoo Community Foundation All-in-One Scholarship
scholarships.description: One online application on the Kaleidoscope portal matches students to more than 60 scholarships and multi-year education grants for college, graduate school, and career training. Open regardless of citizenship or residency status; FAFSA generally required.

scholarships.name: Battle Creek Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 350 scholarships are available annually for high school students, adult learners, post-graduate education, and vocational and trade programs through the Battle Creek Community Foundation, with a single application window each winter.

scholarships.name: Midland Area Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for high school seniors in Midland and Gladwin counties administered through the Midland Area Community Foundation, awarded through a common local application.

scholarships.name: Gerber Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for graduating high school seniors from select high schools in Newaygo, Muskegon, or Oceana counties in West Michigan.

scholarships.name: Rosa L. Parks Scholarship
scholarships.description: Non-renewable scholarship for Michigan high school seniors who reflect Rosa Parks' commitment to social justice and community service while maintaining a strong academic record. Requires an essay and a GPA of 2.5 or above.

scholarships.name: Michigan Council of Women in Technology Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Michigan Council of Women in Technology Foundation
scholarships.description: Scholarship for female Michigan residents enrolled full-time at a Michigan college or university pursuing computer engineering or a related technology field, with a minimum 3.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Kalamazoo Promise
scholarships.description: Place-based scholarship paying up to 100% of tuition at eligible Michigan colleges and universities for graduates of Kalamazoo Public Schools, based on how long the student attended and lived in the district.

scholarships.name: Detroit Promise
scholarships.description: Provides a tuition-free path to trade, two-year, and four-year credentials at Michigan colleges for students who live in Detroit and graduate from a Detroit high school.

scholarships.name: Spartan Tuition Advantage
scholarships.description: Covers the full cost of tuition for qualifying Michigan resident first-year students at Michigan State University who demonstrate financial need. Students are automatically considered after admission; no separate application required.

scholarships.name: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Foundation Student Award Program
scholarships.organization: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Foundation
scholarships.description: Award for medical and doctoral students in Michigan whose research or work aims to improve health care within the state.

scholarships.name: Circle Michigan Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Michigan residents enrolled in a hospitality and tourism program at a Michigan institution with a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Dale and Lynn Bentley Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Michigan environmental scholarship fund (via Access Scholarships)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for undergraduate students at a Michigan college or university pursuing an environmental-related degree, with a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Darooge Family Scholarship for Construction Trades
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school seniors in Kent County with financial need who plan to pursue an undergraduate degree in a construction-related field in Michigan.

scholarships.name: Thelma Orr Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Thelma Orr Memorial Scholarship (via Access Scholarships)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for sophomore undergraduate students pursuing a course of study related to human medicine at any state-accredited Michigan college or university.

scholarships.name: SET Educational Fund Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Michigan residents attending Michigan colleges.

scholarships.name: WID Michigan High School Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Women in Defense Michigan (via Access Scholarships)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for female high school seniors who are Michigan and U.S. residents pursuing STEM degrees at Michigan institutions, with a minimum 3.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: John Weir Academic Scholarship
scholarships.organization: John Weir Academic Scholarship (via Access Scholarships)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school seniors, college freshmen, and college sophomores with disabilities who live in Washtenaw, Livingston, or Monroe County.

scholarships.name: Dr. Lynne Boyle/John Schimpf Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Michigan Association of Broadcasters Foundation (via Access Scholarships)
scholarships.description: Scholarship for second-semester sophomores and above and graduate students majoring in broadcasting, video production, or media at Michigan community colleges and universities.

scholarships.name: Detroit Economic Club Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating high school seniors in Wayne, Oakland, or Macomb counties who have overcome hardships to achieve their personal goals, administered through the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan.

scholarships.name: Ordonez Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for graduating high school seniors who are residents of southwest Detroit and attend eligible southwest Detroit high schools, administered through the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan.

scholarships.name: Michigan First Credit Union Scholarship Competition
scholarships.description: Annual competition awarding up to $85,000 total, with individual awards up to $10,000, to high school seniors and current college or technical students with a minimum 3.0 GPA. Applicants must be Michigan First Credit Union members in good standing.

scholarships.name: Equan Bedenfield Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school seniors who are Genesee County residents with a minimum 3.0 GPA.

scholarships.name: Go Blue Crew Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for high school seniors at specific Michigan high schools with a minimum 3.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: Michigan Future of the Arts Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for BIPOC Michigan students majoring in art or design, open to high school seniors and undergraduates.

scholarships.name: Bill Kuhn Science Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for first-generation Michigan high school seniors pursuing a science major.

scholarships.name: Dr. William and Jo Sherwood Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Michigan residents who are high school seniors or undergraduate students.

scholarships.name: Hopke Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for LGBTQIA+ Michigan high school seniors.

scholarships.name: 100 Women Giving Back Northwoods Scholarship
scholarships.description: Scholarship for Michigan high school seniors with public service and volunteer experience.

scholarships.name: Golden LEAF Scholarship (Colleges and Universities)
scholarships.organization: Golden LEAF Foundation / NC State Education Assistance Authority
scholarships.description: Renewable scholarship for graduating North Carolina high school seniors from qualifying rural counties who plan to attend a participating four-year NC college or university. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA and financial need shown by a FAFSA Student Aid Index of 15,000 or less.

scholarships.name: Golden LEAF Community College Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Golden LEAF Foundation / NC State Education Assistance Authority
scholarships.description: Need-based award for students from qualifying rural North Carolina counties attending a North Carolina community college. Administered through participating campus financial aid offices.

scholarships.name: Next NC Scholarship
scholarships.organization: College Foundation of North Carolina / NC State Education Assistance Authority
scholarships.description: Combined federal and state aid guaranteeing at least $3,000 at a community college or $5,000 at a UNC System university for North Carolina residents with an adjusted gross income of $80,000 or less. Awarded automatically after filing the FAFSA.

scholarships.name: NC Need-Based Scholarship for Private College Students
scholarships.description: State grant for North Carolina residents enrolled full time at an eligible private college or university in the state who demonstrate financial need through the FAFSA. Awarded through the campus financial aid office.

scholarships.name: North Carolina Community Foundation Universal Scholarship Application
scholarships.description: One universal application matches North Carolina students to more than 130 named scholarship funds across the state. In 2025 the foundation awarded over $3 million to more than 500 students. Supplemental questions and recommendation letters may be required for individual funds.

scholarships.name: Achievement Scholarship for Refugees and Immigrants of Wake County
scholarships.description: Supports first-generation U.S. citizens, refugees, or immigrants who are Wake County residents, completed at least one high school year in the county, and plan to attend college full time in North Carolina. Requires a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: James M. Schooler, Sr. Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a graduating African-American male senior from a Durham County or Orange County high school in North Carolina.

scholarships.name: Carol Ann Beerstecher Nursing Scholarship
scholarships.description: For nursing students who have been residents of one of five specified North Carolina counties for at least 12 months, with a minimum 2.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need.

scholarships.name: Carolyn Lemmond Winchester Scholarship
scholarships.description: For a graduating senior at Brevard High School or Rosman High School in Transylvania County, North Carolina.

scholarships.name: Charles Harrison Smith, III Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduating seniors from Apex High School in North Carolina who plan to attend a competitive university majoring in engineering, business, or math.

scholarships.name: Elizabeth Marie Roberts Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Durham County, North Carolina graduating seniors with a minimum 2.5 GPA and demonstrated financial need, with preference for students pursuing health-related careers.

scholarships.name: Felicia Brewer Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: For immigrant or first-generation students from Chapel Hill-Carrboro or Chatham County schools in North Carolina who have overcome significant adversity.

scholarships.name: GSK Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: For residents of four specified North Carolina counties for at least one year who plan to attend an NC public university or community college and show potential to succeed despite adversity.

scholarships.name: iContact Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For iContact employees and their children, or residents of four specified North Carolina counties, majoring in computer science, business, economics, or marketing.

scholarships.name: Jason & Jessica Evans Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: For graduating high school seniors at Orange High School in Hillsborough, North Carolina with a minimum 3.0 GPA and demonstrated financial need.

scholarships.name: Advocates for African Americans Carolinas Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive academic award for African American high school seniors in North Carolina and South Carolina who show outstanding academic achievement and leadership potential.

scholarships.name: Winston-Salem Foundation Scholarships (One-Stop Application)
scholarships.description: A single application checks eligibility for more than 160 need-based and merit-based funds for residents of Davidson, Davie, Forsyth, Stokes, Surry, Wilkes, or Yadkin counties in North Carolina. The application opens January 1 each year.

scholarships.name: Michael Olof Paulson Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to enrolled members of the Lumbee Tribe of North Carolina in memory of Michael Olof Paulson. Applications for the 2026 cycle opened in August 2026.

scholarships.name: Lumbee Tribe Tribal Scholarships
scholarships.description: Named awards including the Kernice Lee Locklear, Dr. Ruth Dial Woods, and Mrs. Agnes Chavis scholarships for Lumbee high school and college students. The tribe distributes nearly $100,000 in scholarships annually.

scholarships.name: Lumbee River EMC Four-Year Scholarships
scholarships.description: The Lucy Smith, John S. O'Briant, Thomas Wade Bethea, and Elias Rogers scholarships award high school seniors attending accredited four-year colleges. Applicants or a parent must be a Lumbee River EMC member.

scholarships.name: Lumbee River EMC J.W. Hunt Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors attending accredited four-year institutions, with preference for students pursuing an agri-business curriculum. Applicants or a parent must be a Lumbee River EMC member.

scholarships.name: Lumbee River EMC J. McN. Gillis Scholarship
scholarships.description: For high school seniors and non-traditional students attending two-year colleges or technical schools. Applicants or a parent must be a Lumbee River EMC member.

scholarships.name: Duke Energy Hispanics in Engineering Scholarship
scholarships.description: For North Carolina residents of Hispanic background who are graduating high school seniors or graduated within the past two years, enrolling in chemical, civil, electrical, mechanical, or nuclear engineering at an NC college with a minimum 2.5 GPA.

scholarships.name: North Carolina Hispanic College Fund Scholarship
scholarships.organization: North Carolina Society of Hispanic Professionals
scholarships.description: For North Carolina residents of Hispanic background who are graduating high school seniors or graduated within the past two years, with a minimum 2.5 GPA, an essay, and a commitment to public service. Applications typically open November 15.

scholarships.name: Morehead-Cain Scholarship
scholarships.description: A merit scholarship covering full tuition, housing, meals, and fees for four years at UNC-Chapel Hill plus four funded summer experiences. North Carolina self-nominees apply directly through the Morehead-Cain website.

scholarships.name: Park Scholarships
scholarships.description: A four-year merit scholarship at NC State based on scholarship, leadership, service, and character. Requires a minimum unweighted 3.8 GPA and applies to entering first-year students.

scholarships.name: Levine Scholars Program
scholarships.organization: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
scholarships.description: A four-year full scholarship at UNC Charlotte covering tuition, housing, meals, and fees plus four funded summer experiences. Selection emphasizes academic excellence, ethical leadership, and community service.

scholarships.name: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program
scholarships.organization: Robertson Scholars Leadership Program (Duke and UNC-Chapel Hill)
scholarships.amountLabel: Full ride at Duke and UNC-Chapel Hill
scholarships.description: A full merit scholarship funding undergraduate study across both Duke University and UNC-Chapel Hill, including a semester living at the partner campus and funded summer experiences.

scholarships.name: SECU Foundation People Helping People Scholarship
scholarships.description: A four-year scholarship for North Carolina public high school seniors accepted to a UNC System campus, with a minimum 2.5 GPA. Applicant or a parent must be a SECU member. Recognizes leadership, integrity, and community involvement.

scholarships.name: NC Farm Bureau R. Flake Shaw Scholarship
scholarships.description: Renewable four-year university scholarships (and two-year community college awards) for rising freshmen who intend to pursue a career in agriculture or an agricultural-related field.

scholarships.name: North Carolina 4-H Development Fund Scholarships
scholarships.organization: North Carolina 4-H Youth Development (NC State Extension)
scholarships.description: Multiple named awards for graduating 4-H members enrolling at a four-year NC college or an NC junior or community college, based on 4-H participation, academic record, and in some cases financial need.

scholarships.name: Robert H. Short Scholars Program
scholarships.description: A last-dollar scholarship for Cumberland County, North Carolina students attending any four-year nonprofit college. Scoring weights academic achievement, community service or work history, and demonstrated financial need equally. Apply in November.

scholarships.name: Cumberland Community Foundation Community Scholarship Program
scholarships.description: One application matches students from southeastern North Carolina to more than a million dollars in named scholarship funds each year. Apply in February.

scholarships.name: WNC Regional Scholarships
scholarships.organization: The Community Foundation of Western North Carolina
scholarships.description: The foundation manages about 50 scholarship funds for students across 18 Western North Carolina counties. A single online application matches students to eligible awards; two recommendation letters are required.

scholarships.name: Hubert B. Humphrey Scholarship
scholarships.organization: North Carolina Bar Association Young Lawyers Division
scholarships.description: Need-based awards for children of slain or permanently disabled North Carolina law enforcement personnel, which may cover tuition, books, or room and board at colleges and technical schools.

scholarships.name: Duke Energy Electrical and Computer Engineering Electric Power Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Duke Energy Foundation / North Carolina State University
scholarships.description: Awarded through NC State to electrical and computer engineering students pursuing the electric power field. Applicants complete the NC State general scholarship application.

scholarships.name: Tuition Aid Grant (TAG)
scholarships.organization: NJ Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
scholarships.description: New Jersey's need-based Tuition Aid Grant supports nearly one-third of all full-time undergraduates in the state. Award varies by financial need, cost of attendance, and available funding. Requires 12 consecutive months of NJ residency and full-time enrollment at an approved NJ college.

scholarships.name: NJ STARS (Student Tuition Assistance Reward Scholarship)
scholarships.organization: NJ Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
scholarships.description: Provides New Jersey's highest achieving students free tuition at their home county college. Students in the top 15 percent of their high school class with a GPA of at least 3.25 qualify, for NJ residents in households earning less than 250,000 dollars.

scholarships.name: Governor's Urban Scholarship Program (GUS)
scholarships.organization: NJ Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
scholarships.description: Merit award for high-achieving New Jersey seniors with financial need from designated high-need communities such as Newark, Camden, Trenton, Paterson, and Jersey City. Requires top 5 percent class rank, a GPA of 3.0 or higher, and 12 months of NJ residency.

scholarships.name: Community College Opportunity Grant (CCOG)
scholarships.organization: NJ Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
scholarships.description: Allows eligible New Jersey students to pursue their first associate degree tuition-free at a county college. Award is need-based and applied after other state and federal grants. Students apply through NJFAMS with the FAFSA or NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application.

scholarships.name: Garden State Guarantee (GSG)
scholarships.organization: NJ Higher Education Student Assistance Authority (HESAA)
scholarships.description: Need-based program that makes college more affordable for students in their third and fourth years at New Jersey public four-year institutions. Tier 1 covers students with adjusted gross income between 0 and 65,000 dollars. Applied through the NJFAMS system.

scholarships.name: Elizabeth A. Allen / Isabelle M. Hickman Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a New Jersey public high school senior with a GPA of 3.75 or higher who has been accepted to a four-year college or university. One-year award administered by the New Jersey Retired Educators Association.

scholarships.name: Fred E. Aug Community College Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-year award for a New Jersey public high school senior with a GPA of 2.75 or higher who has been accepted by a community college. Administered by the New Jersey Retired Educators Association.

scholarships.name: Walter P. Krichling Jr. Career & Technical Education Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-year award for a New Jersey public high school senior with a GPA of 2.3 or higher accepted to a trade, vocational, or career and technical education program. Administered by the New Jersey Retired Educators Association.

scholarships.name: Princeton Post No. 76 American Legion Dr. Henry J. Frank Scholarship
scholarships.description: One 4,000 dollar scholarship awarded annually to a student from Princeton, West Windsor, or Plainsboro who is a child, grandchild, or great-grandchild of a U.S. Armed Forces veteran, pursuing undergraduate study at a community college, technical school, or four-year institution.

scholarships.name: William F. Johnson Jr. Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to three awards of approximately 3,000 dollars for Princeton High School graduating seniors who previously attended Princeton Middle School and demonstrate scholarship, leadership, and community service. Funds cover ancillary college expenses such as books and a computer.

scholarships.name: Mary Elliott Wislar Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Two-year scholarship for a Mercer County resident who has demonstrated leadership in school, extracurricular, or community activities, pursuing study at a four-year college, two-year college, or vocational school.

scholarships.name: Lion Woodward Educational Fund (Rotary Club of Trenton)
scholarships.organization: Rotary Club of Trenton via Princeton Area Community Foundation
scholarships.description: Renewable award of up to 4,000 dollars per year for up to four years for a high school student in Trenton or the greater Mercer and Bucks counties area with a minimum 2.0 GPA. Selection weighs financial need, academic achievement, community service, and leadership.

scholarships.name: A. Myrtle Hensor Teaching Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-year award for a Princeton Regional High School student, female preferred, pursuing a career in education at a four-year college, two-year college, or vocational school.

scholarships.name: Louise Maas Allied Health Professions Scholarship
scholarships.description: One-year award for a Princeton Regional High School student, female preferred, pursuing a career in the allied health professions at a four-year college, two-year college, or vocational school.

scholarships.name: Dominique Lisa Pandolfo Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a female New Jersey graduating high school senior who demonstrates strong character and leadership. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: David H. Roe Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a student from the greater Newark area with an interest in math or science who demonstrates financial need. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Bego Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a graduating senior from a recently immigrated family who is a resident of New Jersey, New York, or Pennsylvania. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Peter Eisen Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a student who lost a biological parent before age 18 and maintains a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Vincent P. Arabia Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a New Jersey resident who is physically disabled or blind, with preference for students in South Jersey and Burlington County. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: R. D. Hinsch Collegiate Sailing Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a student with an active sailing interest, paid as 3,000 dollar annual installments up to a 12,000 dollar total. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Keith Hightower Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a student from the northern New Jersey counties who has participated in a science or math competition. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Elizabeth Loudenslager Clark Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a female student from Camden, Gloucester, Salem, Cumberland, or Cape May counties. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: Alfred J. Speak Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to a student from the greater Newark area, with preference for those affiliated with the Boys & Girls Club or First Presbyterian Church. Part of the Community Foundation of New Jersey scholarships universal application.

scholarships.name: NJIT Honors Merit Award
scholarships.description: Automatic-consideration merit scholarship at NJIT of up to tuition and fees for incoming students admitted to the Albert Dorman Honors College with a GPA of 3.2, renewable for four years. Awarded through the admissions application with no separate form.

scholarships.name: William S. Guttenberg Scholarship
scholarships.description: NJIT scholarship of 2,500 dollars, renewable for four years, serving physically challenged New Jersey students, Paterson residents, and families affected by the September 11 attacks.

scholarships.name: Land Conservancy of New Jersey Scholarship
scholarships.organization: The Land Conservancy of New Jersey (via NJIT)
scholarships.description: Award of 10,000 dollars for a New Jersey resident studying environmental studies with a GPA of 3.3 or higher and 45 or more completed college credits.

scholarships.name: Snyder Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award for a junior or senior in a Construction Management or Construction Engineering Technology program with a GPA of 3.0 or higher who demonstrates financial need.

scholarships.name: Aunt Betty Fund STEM Scholarship
scholarships.description: Award of up to 8,000 dollars for a U.S. citizen in a STEM field graduating by spring 2027. Administered through NJIT financial aid.

scholarships.name: Professional Women in Construction NJ Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Professional Women in Construction - New Jersey (via NJIT)
scholarships.description: Award for a female New Jersey resident pursuing a STEM or construction-related field of study.

scholarships.name: Rutgers-Camden Distinguished Achievement Scholarship
scholarships.description: Top-tier merit scholarship for New Jersey first-year students at Rutgers-Camden of up to 7,500 dollars per year, up to 30,000 dollars over four years, renewable at a 3.0 GPA. Automatic consideration with the admissions application by the priority deadline.

scholarships.name: Rutgers-Camden Meritorious Achievement Scholarship
scholarships.description: Merit scholarship for New Jersey first-year students at Rutgers-Camden of up to 5,000 dollars per year, up to 20,000 dollars over four years, renewable at a 2.75 GPA. Automatic consideration with the admissions application.

scholarships.name: Rutgers-New Brunswick Merit Scholarships
scholarships.description: Competitive merit scholarships for incoming first-year and transfer students at Rutgers-New Brunswick, awarded automatically to qualifying applicants who apply by the December 1 priority deadline with all credentials submitted. No separate application required.

scholarships.name: LUPE Latina Leadership Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Latinas United for Political Empowerment (LUPE Fund)
scholarships.description: Supports young Latina women enrolled at accredited New Jersey colleges or universities who have completed at least one semester. Recipients are selected on academic performance, civic engagement, and financial need.

scholarships.name: Futuro Fund Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Latino Mental Health Association of New Jersey
scholarships.description: Two 5,000 dollar awards, one to a doctoral-level and one to a master's-level student, for New Jersey residents pursuing careers in mental health and committed to serving the Latino community. Recipients attend the LMHANJ annual conference.

scholarships.name: New Jersey Elks Most Valuable Student Scholarship
scholarships.description: Competitive scholarship for high school seniors who are U.S. citizens pursuing a four-year degree, ranging from 1,000 dollars up to 12,500 dollars per year. Applications open August 1 and close November 12, judged on scholarship, financial need, and leadership.

scholarships.name: New Jersey Elks Special Children's Committee Scholarship
scholarships.description: Two 10,000 dollar awards, one female and one male, granted to graduating New Jersey seniors who assist students with disabilities, plus two 4,000 dollar runner-up awards. Administered by the NJ State Elks Special Children's Committee.

scholarships.name: New Jersey Elks Family Scholarship
scholarships.description: 900 dollar scholarships for children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren of New Jersey Elks members. Open to high school seniors as well as college freshmen, sophomores, and juniors.

scholarships.name: Ohio College Opportunity Grant (OCOG)
scholarships.description: State need-based grant for Ohio-resident undergraduates with household income of $96,000 or less and a FAFSA Student Aid Index of 3,750 or less. No separate application is required beyond the FAFSA. Maximum award is $4,000 at public institutions and $5,000 at private nonprofit institutions.

scholarships.name: Choose Ohio First Scholarship
scholarships.description: Statewide scholarship for Ohio residents pursuing a certificate or degree in an eligible STEM discipline at a participating Ohio college or university. Students apply through their institution, which sets award amounts and deadlines. The award does not need to be repaid.

scholarships.name: Ohio War Orphan & Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship
scholarships.description: Tuition assistance for children of deceased or severely disabled Ohio veterans who served during a period of declared war or conflict. Applicants must be Ohio residents ages 16 to 24 enrolled full-time for an associate or bachelor's degree at an eligible Ohio institution. Applications must be received or postmarked by May 15.

scholarships.name: The Columbus Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One universal online application gives central Ohio students access to more than 100 scholarship funds. A common requirement is a one-page essay about the applicant's chosen major and what a scholarship would mean to them. The minimum award is $500; the 2026 deadline was extended to March 9.

scholarships.name: Cleveland Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.organization: Cleveland Foundation (via College Now Greater Cleveland)
scholarships.description: The Cleveland Foundation administers 60-plus scholarship funds for Greater Cleveland and Northeast Ohio students, managed through College Now Greater Cleveland's scholarship portal with one common application. Funds support graduating high school seniors and current college students; the 2026 deadline was March 11.

scholarships.name: Greater Cincinnati Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Greater Cincinnati-area high school graduates with a cumulative unweighted GPA of 2.8 or above entering their first year at an accredited two- to four-year institution full-time. Awards are based on academic performance, financial need, and application quality.

scholarships.name: Greater Cincinnati African American Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: Awards for African American high school seniors in the Greater Cincinnati area. Up to ten scholarships ranging from $2,000 to $10,000 are awarded each cycle to students continuing to higher education.

scholarships.name: Cincinnati Scholarship Foundation Awards
scholarships.description: Need-based scholarships for Greater Cincinnati students. Applicants create an account and submit transcripts and a FAFSA Submission Summary showing their Student Aid Index. The 2026-2027 application window ran through April 30.

scholarships.name: The Dayton Foundation ScholarshipCONNECT
scholarships.description: A single application matches Greater Dayton students to more than 300 scholarship opportunities. Graduating high school seniors and current college students from Montgomery, Miami, Greene, Darke, Preble, and northern Warren counties are eligible. Awards range from one-time $1,000 grants to $10,000 renewable scholarships.

scholarships.name: Greater Toledo Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: One universal application matches northwest Ohio and southeast Michigan students to more than 50 scholarship funds; the foundation awards over 400 scholarships annually across 70-plus funds. Awards are based on merit, need, and activities. Universal application deadline is February 11.

scholarships.name: Stark Community Foundation General Scholarship
scholarships.description: Students from Stark and Carroll counties complete one general application that auto-matches them to qualifying funds. Requirements include a FAFSA Submission Summary, a transcript, and two references. The 2026-2027 cycle ran December 15 through April 1.

scholarships.name: Foundation for Appalachian Ohio Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 50 scholarship funds support students across the 32-county Appalachian region of Ohio. The 2026 general application ran January 5 through February 15 with a single online application for most funds.

scholarships.name: Akron Community Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: More than 100 named scholarship funds serve students across Summit, Medina, Portage, Stark, and Wayne counties and specific Akron-area school districts. Students apply through the foundation's online scholarship system; deadlines vary by fund with many near the end of March.

scholarships.name: Ohio News Media Foundation Minority Scholarship
scholarships.description: For minority Ohio high school seniors planning a career in the newspaper industry, especially advertising, communications, journalism, or marketing. Requires a GPA of 2.5 or higher and a 500- to 750-word autobiography describing academic and career interests and journalism-related activities.

scholarships.name: Ohio News Media Foundation University Journalism Scholarship
scholarships.description: Awarded to Ohio college students pursuing journalism at an Ohio university to support future careers in the news industry. Administered by the Ohio News Media Foundation alongside its minority scholarship.

scholarships.name: Ohio 4-H Scholarships
scholarships.description: Two dozen-plus state 4-H scholarships for graduating high school seniors and college students active in Ohio 4-H. OSU-bound students apply through Scholarship Universe; others use a separate link. Priority deadline February 15.

scholarships.name: Ohio Elks Association Legacy Scholarship
scholarships.description: Up to eight scholarships awarded to Ohio students who are children or grandchildren of Elks members in good standing. Administered through the national Elks Legacy Awards program; the 2026 deadline was February 2.

scholarships.name: Ohio Elks Association Vocational Scholarship
scholarships.description: Six $1,000 scholarships (one per Ohio Elks district) for students pursuing advanced training at a technology center, specialty school, training center, or other approved vocational program.

scholarships.name: American Legion Department of Ohio Scholarships
scholarships.description: Scholarships for Ohio students who are Legionnaires in good standing or direct descendants of a current or deceased Legionnaire in good standing, to help offset higher-education costs.

scholarships.name: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Ohio Scholarships
scholarships.organization: American Legion Auxiliary Department of Ohio
scholarships.description: One $1,500 and one $1,000 scholarship awarded annually to Ohio students preparing to enter their freshman year of college, connected to American Legion Auxiliary membership and veterans' families.

scholarships.name: Marathon Petroleum Youth Leadership Awards
scholarships.description: Twenty $2,500 scholarships for outstanding young leaders (ages 14-25) attending school in fall of the award year, headquartered in Findlay, Ohio. Requires a personal response of up to 500 words, a transcript, and a resume of honors and leadership activities.

scholarships.name: OMACCS LEADS! Scholarship
scholarships.description: Open to current high school seniors graduating from any Ohio or Michigan high school by June of the award year. Each applicant may apply for up to three scholarships within the program, administered through LEAF Ohio.

scholarships.name: Horatio Alger Ohio Scholarship
scholarships.description: State-specific award for Ohio high school juniors who have shown perseverance in overcoming adversity, a strong commitment to pursuing a bachelor's degree, and financial need. Administered in Ohio through LEAF.

scholarships.name: Ohio Reach Scholarship
scholarships.description: Supports Ohio students who have experienced foster care and are pursuing postsecondary education. Administered through LEAF Ohio to help current and former foster youth cover college costs.

scholarships.name: Andy Nowacki Foundation Scholarship
scholarships.description: For Northeast Ohio students pursuing careers as peace officers, firefighters, EMTs, or nurses at Northeast Ohio institutions. Deadline is October 31.

scholarships.name: American Legion Ohio Warriors Scholarship Fund
scholarships.description: For dependents of Ohio service members killed in action, to support their higher-education costs. Minimum award $1,000; deadline December 31.

scholarships.name: Ginny Biada Memorial Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Ginny Biada Memorial Scholarship (via LEAF Ohio)
scholarships.description: For undergraduate students from Ohio who identify as low-income and have nonprofit or volunteering experience. Deadline late May.

scholarships.name: Marcia LaRiche Scholarship
scholarships.description: For dependent children of a parent diagnosed with ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) living in Northeast Ohio, to support college education.

scholarships.name: The Columbus Promise Scholarship
scholarships.organization: I Know I Can / City of Columbus / Columbus State
scholarships.description: Covers tuition and fees at Columbus State Community College after Pell and other aid, plus $500 per semester for expenses for up to six semesters, for Columbus City Schools graduates. Students complete the FAFSA, apply to Columbus State, and upload documents through I Know I Can.

scholarships.name: Ohio State Land Grant Opportunity Scholarship
scholarships.description: Covers the full cost of attendance for entering freshmen who are Ohio residents, Pell-eligible, and academically strong (minimum 3.0 GPA). Ohio residents who apply and complete the FAFSA are automatically considered; the November 1 early action deadline is strongly recommended.

scholarships.name: Ohio State Morrill Scholarship Program
scholarships.amountLabel: In-state tuition to full cost of attendance
scholarships.description: Competitive merit and leadership scholarship for high school seniors admitted to Ohio State's Columbus campus who contribute to diversity through scholarship, leadership, service, and civic engagement. Award levels range from in-state tuition (Excellence) up to full cost of attendance (Distinction). Applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal permanent residents.

scholarships.name: ALCOA Fund Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Cleveland Foundation (via College Now Greater Cleveland)
scholarships.description: Awarded to a Black or Hispanic graduate of designated Cleveland high schools, renewable for up to four years. Administered through the Cleveland Foundation scholarship portal at College Now Greater Cleveland; deadline typically mid-March.

scholarships.name: Ohio FFA Foundation Scholarships
scholarships.description: Multiple scholarships for current Ohio FFA members who are high school seniors or college freshmen at the time of application, awarded through one application. The window opens November 1 and closes February 1.

scholarships.name: Ohio State Society DAR Wings of Eagles Scholarship
scholarships.organization: Ohio Society Daughters of the American Revolution
scholarships.description: For legal residents of Ohio, awarded on academic excellence and character. All applicants must be sponsored by an Ohio DAR chapter. Application deadline is January 31.

scholarships.name: Cincinnati Scholarship Foundation (Greater Cincinnati Foundation Fund)
scholarships.description: Additional named scholarship funds administered by the Greater Cincinnati Foundation for area students, matched through the foundation's online scholarship search. Eligibility and deadlines vary by individual fund.
